claims.text: As-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi thin films or nanoribbons have a relatively disordered microstructure.
Mild post-deposition annealing induces partial nanocluster formation in FeMnNiGeSi nanoscale films.
Annealing parameters can be kept low enough to form nanoclusters without causing complete phase segregation or excessive bulk diffusion.
Annealing-induced nanoclusters locally modify magnetic exchange networks.
Annealing-induced nanoclusters reduce magnetostriction-related lattice strain.
Mild annealing will sharpen the magnetic entropy-change peak relative to the as-deposited state.
Mild annealing will narrow the effective temperature range of the magnetic entropy-change response.
Mild annealing will reduce magnetic hysteresis during low-field cooling cycles relative to the as-deposited state.
As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi films or nanoribbons have a broad magnetocaloric response.
As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi films or nanoribbons exhibit significant hysteresis under low-field cycling.
Heat-transfer-rate limitations are significant under the proposed magnetic-cooling operating conditions.
The shape, maximum, and full width at half maximum of the entropy-change-versus-temperature curve are relevant magnetocaloric performance observables.
Magnetization-field loops can be used to assess hysteretic losses.
Quantitative nanoscale data are too limited to specify the magnitude of peak sharpening, hysteresis reduction, or optimal annealing conditions.
The hypothesis is restricted to nanoscale films or nanoribbons, low-field cycling, and annealing that avoids cluster overgrowth and complete phase segregation.

contradictions.description: The boundary excludes annealing that causes excessive phase segregation, but the falsification rule treats observation of excessive segregation as falsifying the mechanism. Such segregation instead indicates that the intervention left the hypothesis's stated operating domain and therefore is not by itself a decisive test of the within-boundary mechanism.
